 OCT. 26, 2026 | UPDATE: It is the final week of early voting for the midterm elections in Tennessee and Georgia.
 Voter turnout in Georgia continues breaking records.
 Here’s how many residents have voted early as of Saturday, October 24:
 Georgia : 1,669,880
 Tennessee : 815,354
 Tennessee last reported early voting statistics on Saturday, with the Secretary of State’s office reporting a 16.97% voter turnout.
 As of Monday morning, October 26, Georgia has seen a total of 1,794,141 early voters, including absentee votes. The Secretary of State’s office reports a 23.8% voter turnout thus far.
 Tennessee has seen fewer voters overall than in 2018 but more than in 2022. So far, Tennessee has seen 51.89% more early voters than in 2022 and 15.76% fewer early voters than in 2018.
 Early voting runs through October 29 in Tennessee and through October 30 in Georgia.
 Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
 OCT. 21, 2026 | PREVIOUS STORY: Early voting numbers in Georgia were twice the amount of Tennessee’s as of Tuesday, October 20, 2026. More than a million ballots have been accepted in Georgia, with less than 500,000 accepted in Tennessee.
 Georgia has surpassed one million in-person votes, with the secretary of state dubbing it a “record-breaking turnout.”
 Early voting information for residents of Hamilton County, TN 
 Here’s where you can vote early in Hamilton County.
 As of noon on Tuesday, 1,007,015 Georgians had voted early for the midterm elections. At the same point in 2022, only 894,412 Georgians had voted early.
 Additionally, 48,916 absentee ballots have been accepted so far in Georgia.
 That brings the total number of votes so far in Georgia to 1,055,931.
 In Tennessee, 490,534 people have cast their vote early as of Tuesday.
 UPDATE: Early voting begins soon in GA, TN for Nov. 3 general election 
 Both Tennessee and Georgia voters will head to the booths on November 3 to elect the next governor.
 The number includes 27,032 early votes recorded in Hamilton County.
 To compare the two states, Georgia has the eighth-highest population at more than 11.3 million residents. Tennessee has the 15th highest population, with more than 7.3 million residents.
 Georgia reports voting numbers more frequently than Tennessee. The Georgia secretary of state’s website provides an Election Data Hub , which states that 1,171,899 ballots had been accepted statewide as of 11:30am on Wednesday, October 21.
 Tennessee does not offer this same feature, and their last reported early voting numbers were from noon on Tuesday.
 Early voting runs through October 29 in Tennessee and through October 30 in Georgia.
 Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
